inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the statements and flows. Cost of equity 8.5%: 10y JGB c. 1.7%, ERP 6.0%, beta 1.0 for a defensive convenience retailer whose flows are c. 80% USD-denominated (7-Eleven Inc./Speedway) and carried in JPY -- the extra beta over a pure Japanese staple is the FX/translation and fuel-margin exposure, charged here and NOT again in the scenarios. After-tax cost of debt c. 1.5% (FY2026 interest expense + interest on bonds JPY49.5bn on c. JPY2.3trn = 2.1% pre-tax, 29% tax). Weights at market: equity JPY4.94trn / debt JPY2.27trn = 69/31. WACC = 0.69 x 8.5 + 0.31 x 1.5 = 6.3%, rounded up to 6.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality and execution risk live in the driver paths.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Of the JPY1,612bn lease obligations at 31 May 2026, all but c. JPY44bn are ASC 842 operating leases of 7-Eleven Inc. (yuho p.14111-14121: lease obligations ex-ASU 2016-02 are 10,238 current + 34,210 non-current). Operating lease cost is a single straight-line charge inside SG&A, i.e. already inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. The small finance-lease principal (financing CF 'Other', c. JPY12-15bn/yr) plus its interest is charged through lease_cost_pct_path at 0.12% of revenue. Not charged twice: D&A for EBIT includes finance-lease ROU depreciation only, which is why it is charged as a cash lease line rather than via capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests of JPY27,618m (31 May 2026) are deducted once in the equity bridge. Post-deconsolidation NCI is immaterial (Q1 FY2027 NCI share of profit JPY252m).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US, with the adaptations file applied -- JPY WACC, one lease treatment, NCI once, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. PERIMETER: FY2026 is the last year carrying H1 of YORK Holdings (superstores, sold to Bain 1 Sep 2025) and Seven Bank (equity-method from 24 Jun 2025); the forward build is anchored on the FY2027 guidance for the pure convenience-store entity (revenue 10,430,000; operating income 425,000; EBITDA 928,000; EPS 120.89), not on a blend across the break. EBITDA here is the company definition: operating income + D&A + goodwill amortisation (JPY137.9bn/yr, non-cash, Speedway/SEI goodwill amortised under J-GAAP), and da_pct_path covers BOTH D&A and goodwill amortisation so that EBIT ties to reported operating income (FY2026: 942,892 - 382,009 - 137,890 = 422,993 = reported OP). Sale-and-leaseback proceeds (JPY143.6bn FY2026, 130.0bn FY2025) are NOT netted against gross capex -- conservative, since the leased-back rent is already in EBITDA; this is unmodelled upside of roughly JPY1bn/yr of FCF per 1% of capex. The equity-method stakes (Seven Bank; 35.07% of K.K. BCJ-95 = YORK successor) and listed cross-holdings sit in 'Investments in securities' JPY356,985m; their income (equity-method P&L, dividends) is below operating income and so outside the flows, hence they are added once in the equity bridge at book value (matching-asset rule). Couche-Tard's c. USD47bn approach was withdrawn July 2025; no control premium is modelled and the terminal cap multiples (13/15/17x FCF) sit at or below today's c. 16x EV/unlevered FCF. Cash taxes: FY2027 guidance implies c. 28% (ordinary 390 -> NI 278); FY2026 current tax 114,352 on EBIT 422,993; 29% used on EBIT, held flat -- part of the goodwill amortisation is tax-deductible in the US (company's EPS-before-goodwill note nets a tax effect), which the flat rate absorbs.

base.narrative: Y1 = FY2027 guidance (revenue flat at 10.43trn on the reported base, EBITDA 928bn = 8.9%, D&A+goodwill 503bn = 4.82%). Thereafter 2% nominal: Japan +3-4% (c. 1,000 net new stores by FY2030, pricing) offset by a North American store base shrinking c. 440 net in FY2026 and flat-to-down merchandise comps, fuel flat. EBITDA margin drifts up 40bp over five years as North Star closes the loss-making tail of the US estate and SEI's overseas OP guidance (+21.5% FY2027) partly sticks; domestic CVS OP assumed to stop eroding at c. 224bn. Capex eases from 3.9% to 3.7% once the FY2026-27 remodel/large-format wave passes. Gordon at 6.5%/1.5% would be 20x; the 15x cap binds -- consistent with today's c. 16x.

bull.narrative: North Star works: US merchandise comps turn positive by FY2028 on fresh food/7NOW/large-format stores, the closed tail lifts SEI's margin, Japan's Live Meal/Seven Cafe investments restore domestic CVS OP growth, and Europe adds a fourth pillar. EBITDA margin reaches 10.2% (still below the FY2024 9.2% consolidated level plus the mix benefit of shedding 2-3% margin superstores). A North American IPO in FY2027-28 crystallises a higher multiple: cap 17x, still only modestly above today's.

bear.narrative: The FY2027 guidance holds only because of fuel margins and a weaker yen; underneath, 7-Eleven Inc. keeps losing merchandise share to Wawa/Sheetz/Buc-ee's/Casey's, FY2028-29 revenue falls as closures continue without the promised remodel uplift, and domestic CVS OP keeps drifting down (250.5bn FY2024 -> 222.5bn FY2026). Margin settles at 8.2%, capex stays at 4.0% to defend the estate, the IPO never happens and the market pays 13x for a shrinking fuel-exposed retailer. Not a solvency case: net debt/EBITDA stays c. 2x.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-restructuring Seven & i is a pure convenience-store operator earning c. JPY425bn of operating income on JPY10.4trn of revenue, 80% of it in North America. The base case takes the FY2027 guidance at face value, lets the North Star closures lift the EBITDA margin 40bp over five years, grows revenue 2% nominal thereafter, and caps the terminal at 15x owner FCF (below today's c. 16x). The axes that matter are US merchandise comps, fuel margin, and whether domestic CVS profit has bottomed.
scenario_narratives.bull: US turnaround delivers positive comps and a 10%+ EBITDA margin, Japan's premium food investments reaccelerate domestic CVS profit, Europe becomes a fourth pillar, and a North American IPO plus the JPY2trn buyback re-rate the equity to 17x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural US share loss and demographic decline in Japan outrun the self-help; revenue shrinks FY2028-29, margins compress to 8.2% while capex to defend the estate stays at 4% of revenue, and the stock trades at 13x a shrinking cash flow.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: North American merchandise comps have been negative for two years, chain sales fell 7.3% in FY2026, domestic CVS operating income has eroded for three years, and the turnaround is being run by a new management team whose first big catalyst (the North American IPO) has already slipped. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: US comps, Japan margin, and a re-rating event. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A defensive, cash-generative franchisor/retailer discounted at a JPY-built 6.5% WACC with the terminal value capped at 13-17x owner FCF rather than left to Gordon. Buybacks are value-neutral (flat share count, SBC expensed); value comes from whether the North American estate stops shrinking and the margin recovers. A 15% hurdle on a 6.5%-WACC asset necessarily puts the entry price well below intrinsic value.
key_risks_to_valuation: North American merchandise same-store sales stay negative and the store-closure program does not lift SEI's margin
Fuel margin normalisation: FY2027 guidance was raised on Q1 fuel margins, which are not a recurring driver
Yen strength: c. 80% of revenue and most of EBITDA are USD-denominated; guidance assumes USD/JPY 157
Domestic convenience-store operating income continues its three-year decline as Japan's population shrinks
Net debt JPY1.6trn plus JPY1.6trn of operating lease obligations; the remaining c. JPY1.4trn buyback commitment is funded from FCF and asset sales
Q1 cash is seasonally flattered by c. JPY150bn of franchisee/settlement deposits; the Aug 2026 balance sheet was not yet extracted
Sale-and-leaseback proceeds (c. JPY130-145bn/yr) are excluded from FCF: conservative, but a change in that practice would change capex intensity
